entry.title: Uppgifter: Branddörrar hindrade polisen att skjuta mot skytten
entry.summary:
• Vid masskjutningen i Örebro besvarade inte de första polispatrullerna skotten från gärningsmannen, eftersom deras vapen inte var kraftfulla nog för att kunna skjuta genom de tre dörrar med förstärkt glas som fanns mellan dem och gärningsmannen. Det uppger Svenska Dagbladet.

  • Rickard Anderssons skott gick igenom glaset på alla tre dörrarna, men poliserna sköt inte tillbaka eftersom de uppges ha vetat att deras vapen inte kunde göra det på ett säkert sätt.

  • Inte heller polisens förstärkningsvapen hade kunnat gå igenom alla tre glasdörrarna, enligt källor till tidningen.

entry.summary:
For the past few days, 7 Inkscape Members met up in Frankfurt, Germany to collaborate on various projects and get to know each other.
We were especially delighted to have two InkStitch maintainers, a major downstream project of Inkscape, join us. This way, we got to learn about the struggles and worries of projects using Inkscape better, and even built a new capability for extensions to interact with Inkscape during the event.
Marc, our release manager, cleared out our merge request backlog, reviewing and merging various contributions. He also set up a new web-based translation service, so that translators don't have to learn how to use git, and we hopefully see better Inkscape translations in many languages. entry.title: Scientists spot tiny Sun jets driving fast and slow solar wind
entry.summary:
Video: 00:00:40
Back in 2023, we reported on Solar Orbiter’s discovery of tiny jets near the Sun’s south pole that could be powering the solar wind. The team behind this research has now used even more data from the European Space Agency’s prolific solar mission to confirm that these jets exist all over dark patches in the Sun’s atmosphere, and that they really are a source of not only fast but also slow solar wind. The newfound jets can be seen in this sped-up video as hair-like wisps that flash very briefly, for example within the circled regions of the Sun's surface. In reality they last around one minute and fling out charged particles at about 100 km/s. entry.title: Wobbling stars reveal hidden companions in Gaia data
ESA’s Gaia finds a mysterious planet and brown dwarf
entry.summary:
Video: 00:01:40
Using data from the European Space Agency’s Gaia mission, scientists have found a huge exoplanet and a brown dwarf. This is the first time a planet has been uniquely discovered by Gaia’s ability to sense the gravitational tug or ‘wobble’ the planet induces on a star. Both the planet and brown dwarf are orbiting low-mass stars, a scenario thought to be extremely rare. Read more.
